purpose: Standardises reporting of coronary artery stenosis and plaque burden on coronary CT angiography, with management suggestions for patients presenting with stable or acute chest pain.
issuer: Society of Cardiovascular Computed Tomography (SCCT), with ACC, ACR and NASCI (expert consensus document)
system: CAD-RADS 2.0 Coronary Artery Disease - Reporting and Data System
aliases: coronary artery disease reporting and data system

inputs.label: CAD-RADS category
inputs.how_stated: the CAD-RADS category as dictated: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4A, 4B, 5 or N, the term before the first slash (N/P2 is N; 3/P2/N is 3). Do not infer it from stenosis percentages.

inputs.label: Clinical presentation
inputs.how_stated: stable for stable chest pain or suspected stable CAD; acute for acute chest pain or suspected ACS (eg emergency department); other when the indication is not chest pain (eg pre-procedural, asymptomatic)

locator.section: 3.1 CAD-RADS categories (Tables 4 and 5 list the categories for stable and for acute chest pain)

inputs.label: Modifier E (non-atherosclerotic cause of the coronary abnormality)
inputs.how_stated: true when the code carries /E or the narrowing has a non-atherosclerotic cause (eg dissection, anomalous origin, aneurysm, vasculitis, fistula, extrinsic compression); false for a code without E in atherosclerotic disease

inputs.label: Plaque burden (P category)
inputs.how_stated: P1 to P4 after the category (eg 'CAD-RADS 2/P3'): mild, moderate, severe or extensive overall plaque

inputs.label: Ischaemia modifier (I) from CT-FFR or stress CT perfusion
inputs.how_stated: from CT-FFR or stress CTP: positive for I+, negative for I-, borderline for I+/- (I±); absent when stated as not performed; not assessable when non-diagnostic

locator.section: 3.3.5 Modifier I = ischemia: CT-FFR or CTP

inputs.label: CT ischaemia test used
inputs.how_stated: ct_ffr for CT-FFR (FFR-CT); ctp for stress myocardial CT perfusion

inputs.label: CT perfusion I- coded for a prior infarct (fixed perfusion defect)
inputs.how_stated: true for a fixed (stress and rest) perfusion defect of prior infarction without ischaemia; false when stress CTP shows no defect

locator.section: 3.1 CAD-RADS categories; 3.3.5 Modifier I; 3.3.6 Modifier E

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS 0: no plaque or stenosis (0%); absence of CAD.
outcomes.recommendation: No further cardiac investigation. Reassurance; consider non-atherosclerotic causes of symptoms.

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS 0: no plaque or stenosis (0%); absence of CAD; ACS highly unlikely.
outcomes.recommendation: No further evaluation of ACS is required; reassurance. If troponin is positive, consider other sources of raised troponin.

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS N: non-diagnostic study; obstructive CAD cannot be excluded.
outcomes.recommendation: Additional or alternative evaluation may be needed.
caveats: CAD-RADS N is used when at least one segment is non-interpretable and interpretable segments show no stenosis ≥50%; with a stenosis ≥50% the numeric category is reported with modifier N (section 3.3.1).

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS N: non-diagnostic study; obstructive CAD cannot be excluded; ACS cannot be excluded.
outcomes.recommendation: Additional or alternative evaluation for ACS is needed.
caveats: CAD-RADS N is used when at least one segment is non-interpretable and interpretable segments show no stenosis ≥50%; with a stenosis ≥50% the numeric category is reported with modifier N (section 3.3.1).

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS 1: minimal stenosis (1-24%) or plaque without stenosis; minimal non-obstructive CAD, P1 plaque burden.
outcomes.recommendation: No further cardiac investigation. Consider non-atherosclerotic causes of symptoms; consider risk factor modification and preventive pharmacotherapy.
caveats: High-risk plaque (two or more high-risk features) signals the need for more aggressive preventive therapy, including in CAD-RADS 1 and 2 (section 3.3.4).

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS 3: moderate stenosis (50-69%).
outcomes.recommendation: Consider functional assessment. Aggressive risk factor modification and preventive pharmacotherapy; anti-anginal therapy should be considered per guideline-directed care.
caveats: Applies when no CT-FFR or CT perfusion was performed, or when it was non-diagnostic (modifier N for CT-FFR or CTP, section 3.3.5.1).
Functional assessment includes CT-FFR, CT perfusion, stress testing (exercise ECG, stress echocardiography, SPECT, PET, cardiac MRI) or invasive FFR (Table 4 footnote c; Table 5 footnote b).
Functional imaging or ICA should be considered to identify a target lesion (if unknown) and if symptoms persist despite adequate medical therapy (Table 4 footnote d).
CAD-RADS 3 with high-risk plaque (excluding left main lesions) should prompt consideration of more aggressive management than CAD-RADS 3 alone, particularly in acute chest pain (section 3.3.4).
Guideline-directed care in the source means the 2021 AHA/ACC chest pain, 2012 ACC/AHA stable ischaemic heart disease and 2019 ACC/AHA prevention guidelines (Table 4 footnote d; Table 5 footnote c).

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS 3: moderate stenosis (50-69%); I+.
outcomes.recommendation: Consider ICA, especially if frequent symptoms persist after guideline-directed medical therapy. Aggressive risk factor modification and preventive pharmacotherapy; anti-anginal therapy should be considered per guideline-directed care.
caveats: For CT-FFR, I+ is a lesion-specific value ≤0.75 in a vessel large enough for PCI, I- is >0.80 and I+/- is 0.76-0.80 (Table 6).
Benefit of revascularisation should be confined to patients with persistent symptoms despite optimal medical therapy (Table 4 footnote e; Table 5 footnote d).
Guideline-directed care in the source means the 2021 AHA/ACC chest pain, 2012 ACC/AHA stable ischaemic heart disease and 2019 ACC/AHA prevention guidelines (Table 4 footnote d; Table 5 footnote c).

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS 3: moderate stenosis (50-69%); I-; CT-FFR >0.80 or stress CTP without a perfusion defect.
outcomes.recommendation: Deferral of ICA would be appropriate; optimise medical therapy. Aggressive risk factor modification and preventive pharmacotherapy.
caveats: Functional imaging or ICA should be considered to identify a target lesion (if unknown) and if symptoms persist despite adequate medical therapy (Table 4 footnote d).
For CT-FFR, I+ is a lesion-specific value ≤0.75 in a vessel large enough for PCI, I- is >0.80 and I+/- is 0.76-0.80 (Table 6).

The deferral advice is in the CT-FFR guidance (section 3.3.5.1, Table 6); for CTP, a negative study excludes ischaemia and avoids further downstream testing (section 3.3.5.2). Library decision: applied to stable chest pain only.
Guideline-directed care in the source means the 2021 AHA/ACC chest pain, 2012 ACC/AHA stable ischaemic heart disease and 2019 ACC/AHA prevention guidelines (Table 4 footnote d; Table 5 footnote c).

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS 3: moderate stenosis (50-69%); I-; CTP fixed perfusion defect from prior infarction.
outcomes.recommendation: No source ICA deferral advice for I- from a fixed infarct; CAD-RADS 3 line applies: consider functional assessment; aggressive risk factor modification and preventive pharmacotherapy.
caveats: A prior infarct with a fixed perfusion defect and no ischaemia is coded I-; document the infarct in the impression (Table 1 footnote a).
Library decision: the Table 4 category line is used unchanged.
Functional assessment includes CT-FFR, CT perfusion, stress testing (exercise ECG, stress echocardiography, SPECT, PET, cardiac MRI) or invasive FFR (Table 4 footnote c; Table 5 footnote b).

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS 3: moderate stenosis (50-69%); I+/-; CT-FFR 0.76-0.80.
outcomes.recommendation: Consider ICA according to symptoms, lesion location and trans-lesional CT-FFR gradient, if likely to benefit from revascularisation. Aggressive risk factor modification and preventive pharmacotherapy.
caveats: For CT-FFR, the trans-lesional gradient (pressure loss from 1-2 cm proximal to 1-2 cm distal to the stenosis) is significant above 0.12 (section 3.3.5.1; Table 6).
For CT-FFR, I+ is a lesion-specific value ≤0.75 in a vessel large enough for PCI, I- is >0.80 and I+/- is 0.76-0.80 (Table 6).
Guideline-directed care in the source means the 2021 AHA/ACC chest pain, 2012 ACC/AHA stable ischaemic heart disease and 2019 ACC/AHA prevention guidelines (Table 4 footnote d; Table 5 footnote c).

outcomes.classification: CAD-RADS 4A: severe stenosis (70-99%).
outcomes.recommendation: Consider ICA or functional assessment. Aggressive risk factor modification and preventive pharmacotherapy; anti-anginal therapy and revascularisation options should be considered per guideline-directed care.
caveats: Applies when no CT-FFR or CT perfusion was performed, or when it was non-diagnostic (modifier N for CT-FFR or CTP, section 3.3.5.1).
Functional assessment includes CT-FFR, CT perfusion, stress testing (exercise ECG, stress echocardiography, SPECT, PET, cardiac MRI) or invasive FFR (Table 4 footnote c; Table 5 footnote b).
Functional imaging or ICA should be considered to identify a target lesion (if unknown) and if symptoms persist despite adequate medical therapy (Table 4 footnote d).
ICA may be favoured with high-grade stenosis (>90%), high-risk plaque features, I+ or concordant ischaemia on other stress tests in a candidate for revascularisation (Table 4 footnote e).
Benefit of revascularisation should be confined to patients with persistent symptoms despite optimal medical therapy (Table 4 footnote e; Table 5 footnote d).
Guideline-directed care in the source means the 2021 AHA/ACC chest pain, 2012 ACC/AHA stable ischaemic heart disease and 2019 ACC/AHA prevention guidelines (Table 4 footnote d; Table 5 footnote c).

summary.text: CAD-RADS 2.0 standardises coronary CT angiography reporting as stenosis category, then plaque burden (P1-P4), then modifiers, with management suggestions for stable and for acute chest pain.
The category is per patient: the most severe (clinically most relevant) luminal stenosis, from CAD-RADS 0 (no plaque or stenosis) to 5 (total occlusion), with N for a non-diagnostic study.
CAD-RADS complements and does not replace the report impression, and its management suggestions do not replace clinical judgement; it is an expert consensus document.

definitions.text: Stenosis grading: 0% no visible stenosis; 1-24% minimal; 25-49% mild; 50-69% moderate; 70-99% severe; 100% occluded.
CAD-RADS 4 is split: 4A is a 70-99% stenosis; 4B is left main stenosis ≥50% or three-vessel obstructive (≥70%) disease.
Plaque burden P1 mild, P2 moderate, P3 severe, P4 extensive; by CAC 1-100, 101-300, 301-999, >1000, or by segment involvement score ≤2, 3-4, 5-7, ≥8, or visually. P is not used with CAD-RADS 0.

Modifier I records a CT ischaemia test (CT-FFR or stress CTP): I+ lesion-specific ischaemia, a reversible perfusion defect or peri-infarct ischaemia (stress defect larger than rest defect); I- negative, including a fixed infarct without ischaemia; I+/- borderline.

Other modifiers: N non-diagnostic, HRP high-risk plaque (two or more of positive remodelling, low attenuation <30 HU, spotty calcification, napkin-ring sign), S stent, G graft, E non-atherosclerotic cause.
Coding order: stenosis category, then P, then modifiers N, HRP, I, S, G, E, separated by slashes (eg CAD-RADS 3/P3/I+).

pitfalls.text: Grade vessels larger than 1.5 mm in diameter; CAD-RADS does not apply to smaller vessels.
Use N as the category only when no interpretable segment has a stenosis ≥50%; otherwise give the numeric category with modifier N (eg 3/P2/N).
A stenosis bypassed by a fully patent graft is not counted; grade grafts and native segments distal to and including the anastomosis.
In-stent stenosis is graded like native stenosis; the category depends on the severe stenosis whether or not it is in a stented vessel.
CAD-RADS is for atherosclerotic disease; non-atherosclerotic narrowing (dissection, anomalous origin, aneurysm, vasculitis, fistula, extrinsic compression) is flagged with modifier E.
In multivessel disease the physiologically significant lesion may not be the most anatomically severe; clarify this in the report and impression.
The recommendations may not apply to every clinical scenario; add comments and convey uncertainty where relevant.
